6 months ago I had a heart attack. Almost died. There's a reality check for you. It woke me up. I found that life is fleeting and tenuous, and I cherish more, and give less fucks. When mortality hits you, this question becomes less important. To answer your question, no, I don't think I do.

Here's the thing... Knowing when you are going to die will influence how you live your life, consequently change when you will die. For example, you might be a relatively cautious person, the magic calculator tells you that you will die in 80 years, so you start taking risks as a result. Consequently, something goes wrong and that changes your life expectancy to 1 year. As such, the calculator would need to perform some sort of iterative calculation (like honing in on a local minima).

More importantly, however, knowing that the calculator would need to take this observer-effect process into account should also affect the result. I.e. if your response to being told that you were going to die in a year was to live life up, the prediction may become a self-fulfilling prophecy. On the other hand, if you reaction was to appreciate that the answer is mutable and dependent on your response, then your decision to live sensibly and healthily despite the bad news may create a paradox in that iteration and result in a different life expectancy.

Of course, there is the possibility the universe acts very much like an evil genie granting a wish. If you are told that you will live for 80 years and you decide to flaunt it by putting a gun to your head and pulling the trigger, you spend the next 80 years as a vegetable in a coma.

All things being equal, I would prefer to know.
